static_traits.name: Wang Yue
static_traits.medical_history: No history of psychological counseling or treatment; No major physical illness history; no similar problems before
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe Anxiety and diet worries; thinking shows catastrophizing, black-and-white and overgeneralization; fairly cooperative in counseling, able to do cognitive restructuring; tense tone, often falling into repeated worries.

basic_info.main_problem: I have been experiencing intense Anxiety related to eating habits and weight gain. This Anxiety began about a week ago, when I ate fast food for several days in a row. I am convinced this eating pattern will make me obese when Approaching winter, and eating fast food will definitely be unhealthy.
basic_info.core_demands: Escalating Anxiety and obsession with weight gain prompting me to seek counseling, to address these cognitive distortions and their impact on my daily life.

core_beliefs: Only strict, perfect eating can guarantee health and no weight gain
Short-term poor eating inevitably leads to serious consequences (obesity and unhealthiness)

special_situations.event: After eating fast food for several consecutive days, repeatedly recalls this diet
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I ate fast food multiple times in a week, I will inevitably gain weight and become unhealthy
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Considering extreme dieting or excessive exercise to 'Undo' the effects of fast food
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will definitely become obese and unhealthy

special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Winter makes it easier to gain weight; if I do not strictly control my diet immediately now, I will inevitably become obese when winter comes
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Sets overly strict dietary rules, trying to avoid fast food completely
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will definitely get fatter when winter comes

special_situations.event: When making food choices (deciding what to eat)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One 'wrong' choice will completely ruin my health and weight management
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Pursuing perfect eating, excessive monitoring and self-reproach, avoiding all 'unhealthy' foods
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I choose wrong once more, I am completely finished

special_situations.event: Focuses attention only on the fast food eaten recently, ignoring other diet and evidence
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Negative evidence matters more than positive; eating poorly recently means everything is bad overall
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly checking and dwelling on fast-food intake, negating any positive or buffering factors
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I have been eating very poorly lately, which means I am already heading toward obesity

core_conflict.wish: Longs to gain health and a sense of safety through a controllable, perfect diet
core_conflict.fear: Fearing losing control leading to obesity, being negated by oneself, life becoming unhealthy
defense_goal: By making rigid rules, strict Self-monitoring to lower Anxiety and avoid 'wrong' choices

object_relations.self_representation: unwilling to expose vulnerability, one who tends to bear Anxiety alone
object_relations.object_representation: others who may not understand or would judge oneself (friends/family)

manifestations: Constraining oneself with rigid eating rules, treating 'eating fast food is definitely unhealthy' as absolute truth
Unable to tolerate one mistaken choice, Demanding oneself with 'must/definitely' rules
outcomes: Reduced enjoyment of autumn and winter seasons, quality of life affected

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Overly cautious when choosing food; worries that making the wrong choice will be a 'complete failure'
Judges oneself by strict rules, tends toward excessive monitoring and self-blame
Unwilling to discuss Anxiety with friends or family, bearing pressure alone

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Treating the rule 'eating fast food inevitably means unhealthy' as absolute truth
using 'must/definitely' language and beliefs to constrain one's choices

positive_force: Able to realize 'logically' that a week of fast food does not necessarily produce catastrophic consequences
Willing to seek counseling to address cognitive distortions and try cognitive restructuring
Willing to set realistic diet and health goals
Has the willingness to carry out concrete plans (for example, planning balanced meals)
negative_force: Cognitive distortions such as catastrophizing, black-and-white thinking, overgeneralization, and mental filtering are prominent
Predictive worries about winter weight and uncertainty hard to bear
Excessive Self-monitoring and self-reproach, using rigid rules to constrain oneself
Low utilization of social support (currently unwilling to discuss Anxiety with relatives and friends)
Attention overly focused on the recent fast-food experience, ignoring positive or neutral evidence

target_behavior.behavior: Excessive Anxiety and Catastrophizing about weight gain and health
antecedent: After eating fast food several days in a row, repeatedly recalls the experience
target_behavior.core_reason: Overgeneralizing short-term poor eating as inevitably leading to obesity and unhealthiness, evaluating oneself with black-and-white rules
target_behavior.function: Through worry and strict Self-monitoring to avoid perceived health risks and consequences, gaining a brief sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Persistent high Anxiety, reducing enjoyment of daily life and autumn/winter seasons, inducing thoughts of extreme dieting or excessive exercise
